solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 13 down, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: King perhaps was concerned with English loss

indicators.note: the English letter suffers a loss, so it is taken out of the word

parts.note: to care is to be concerned, so 'was concerned' is cared

explanation.surface: A monarch who worried about England's decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like a ruler, but the king here sits in a pack of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is one example of a playing card, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Move slowly in cold, finding a fur

indicators.note: the slow movement goes in the cold

parts.note: a chill is a coldness
to inch is to edge forward slowly

explanation.surface: Someone creeping through the cold finds a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' is only a link here; the 'a' belongs to the wordplay, and the definition is just 'fur'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small Andean rodent, prized as fur.

clue.text: What ruler is expecting to lose power?

indicators.note: the power letter is lost from the word

parts.note: to be expecting is to be pregnant
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A riddle about a queen expecting a baby losing her authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, the state of a monarch who currently rules.

clue.text: Elevation of point in orbit around article between rings

indicators.note: the orbital point goes around the rest, holding it inside

parts.note: an apsis is the point of an orbit nearest to or furthest from the body orbited

indicators.note: the article sits between the two rings, so it goes inside them

parts.note: two rings are two O shapes
'the' is the definite article

explanation.surface: An astronomer describes a spacecraft rising to a point of its orbit near a planet's rings.
explanation.walkthrough: An apsis is a technical astronomy term for the nearest or furthest point of an orbit, an unfamiliar word to many solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: Apotheosis is elevation to divine status, the raising of someone to the rank of a god.

clue.text: Dicky, Ron, Peg and Arthur's family

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of names, Dicky, Ron and Peg, joined to King Arthur's family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' poses as a third name; it is the anagram signal. Dicky means shaky or unreliable in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's father was Uther Pendragon, so Pendragon is the surname of his house.

clue.text: Label left on a musical instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the next

parts.note: a tab is a small label attached to something

explanation.surface: A label stuck on the left side of an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabla is a pair of small hand drums used in Indian classical music.

clue.text: End of The Times. End and destruction

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word the is used

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a termination is an end

explanation.surface: Like a doom-laden newspaper headline: the paper's last issue, end and ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times looks like the newspaper, but the words split: 'End of The' gives E, and 'Times' is the times sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: Extermination is utter destruction, the wiping out of a whole population.

clue.text: Old African country in South Africa or one elsewhere

indicators.note: the old letter and the other country go in the abbreviation

parts.note: Mali is another African country, far from South Africa

explanation.surface: A historical African nation, either in the south or somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old African country' looks like one unit, but Old gives O, and 'one elsewhere' is a second African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia is a nation in the Horn of Africa, on the continent's eastern coast.

clue.text: Put in post — collection around noon

indicators.note: the set goes around the noon letter

parts.note: a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: A letter posted for the midday collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collection' looks like the postal pick-up but means a set.
explanation.definitionFit: When a letter has been posted, it has been sent on its way through the mail.

clue.text: Firmly establish new cereal crop on island

indicators.note: the new crop goes on, after, the island letter

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island
grain is a cereal crop such as wheat or barley

explanation.surface: Farmers plan to plant a novel cereal on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingrain something is to fix it deeply, so that a habit or idea becomes firmly set.

clue.text: Run risks with time slippage in job requiring Russian cash

indicators.note: the time letter slips from its place to a later one

parts.note: a task is a job
for as in asking for, so meaning requiring
the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A job for Russian money, with delays, brings risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippage' signals that the time letter drops from the front of the job to a later place in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for trouble is an idiom for behaving in a way that invites danger.

clue.text: Support for transport workers led by one in energy unit

indicators.note: the workers come after, led by, the first part
the letter for one goes in the energy unit

parts.note: BTU is the British thermal unit, a unit of energy
I is the Roman numeral for one
men is a common crossword word for workers

explanation.surface: A transport union's backing is headed by a single member of a power body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport workers' looks like a single phrase for a union; it splits, with 'Support for transport' the definition and 'workers' giving MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitumen is the tar used to surface roads, which carry traffic, so it holds up transport.

clue.text: Plain American code reader needs PIN, say

parts.note: a code cracker reads coded messages
a pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons, so it is an example of a barrel

explanation.surface: A cash machine user needs a personal identification number to read the card.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN in capitals pretends to be a personal identification number; here it is a small beer cask.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage cracker-barrel describes homespun, unsophisticated talk or wisdom, from the barrels round which village store gossips sat.

clue.text: Mere refund that's terrible reason for Brexit?

indicators.note: terrible says the letters are in a bad state, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Complaint that a small refund is an awful reason for leaving the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the definition is loose: the vote was the cause of Britain leaving the EU, not a synonym for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2016 referendum, a popular vote, decided that Britain would leave the European Union.

clue.text: Starting passage with paint roller after stripping down

indicators.note: the words paint roller are pared away at both ends, leaving letters from within them

explanation.surface: A decorator's instructions on using a roller once the old wallpaper has been stripped.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music or writing, a short form of introduction.

clue.text: Shoot a lot of stoat in the northern way

indicators.note: the shortened stoat goes in the way

parts.note: gate is a northern English and Scots word for a way or street

indicators.note: a lot of the word, not all, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the ermine is the stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: A northern hunter shooting a stoat along a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like firing a gun but is the verb for a plant sprouting. The ermine is the stoat in its white winter coat.
explanation.definitionFit: When a seed germinates it sprouts, putting out its first shoot.

clue.text: Concerning attitude, nearly completely calm

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a pose is an attitude struck by the body

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: full means completely, as in full well

explanation.surface: A posture that is almost totally calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Reposeful means full of repose, peaceful and at rest.

clue.text: Relax, mostly understanding the reverse of a long down entry?

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: light means understanding, as in seeing the light

parts.words: the reverse of a long down entry
parts.note: the long down entry is 10 down in this grid, so its reverse is ten up

explanation.surface: A puzzle note on easing off by grasping how the down answers run.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'long down entry' is this puzzle's 10 down, a thirteen-letter answer; the reverse of 'ten down' is 'ten up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is an idiom for becoming less serious and more at ease.

clue.text: Finished tarts after good fish

indicators.note: the finished part and tarts come after the good letter

parts.note: up means finished, as in time is up
tarts are kinds of pie

explanation.surface: Tarts finished off after a good fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Guppies are small tropical freshwater fish, popular in home aquariums.

clue.text: Informed in a note about conflict

indicators.note: a and the note go about, on either side of, the conflict

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A briefing note keeps someone up to date about a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aware means having knowledge of something, so you are well briefed about it.

clue.text: A sin involving hoards, centrally?

indicators.note: the sin involves, or contains, the central letters

parts.note: a vice is a sin

indicators.note: only the central letters of hoards are taken

explanation.surface: A wrongdoing that centres on hoarding wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: greed is a sin that involves hoarding.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed for wealth, one of the seven deadly sins, which leads people to hoard.

clue.text: Arrest action badly after beginning of project?

definitions.text: Arrest action badly after beginning of project?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of project is used
the letters of arrest action are badly arranged, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone who stops working poorly as soon as a project starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a procrastinator halts action once the project has begun.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to put off doing something, delaying work that ought to be done now.

clue.text: Are our large estates all in the middle of the countryside?

indicators.note: each of the five words gives up the letter in its middle

explanation.surface: A question about whether large country estates all lie deep in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the country, as opposed to towns and cities.

clue.text: One such as Escoffier, say, cut short hunger

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the end of the phrase is cut off

parts.note: Auguste Escoffier was a famous French chef

explanation.surface: A great chef like Escoffier briefly staves off appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long for it, a craving like hunger.

clue.text: Mountaineer clubs get ready for action

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
to limber up is to loosen the muscles before exercise

explanation.surface: A climber gathers ice axes and warms up before a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber is someone who scales mountains or rock faces, a mountaineer.

clue.text: Found attractive dace swimming with fin

indicators.note: the letters swim about into a new order

explanation.surface: An angler is taken with a dace swimming by with its fin.
explanation.definitionFit: If you fancied someone, you were drawn to them and liked their looks.

clue.text: Flower favoured by churches retails freely in cathedral

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go in the cathedral name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A cathedral shop sells off the blooms churches like.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city near Cambridge in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The white Easter lily is the bloom traditionally used to decorate churches at Easter.

clue.text: Fish out of river from which scales hang

indicators.note: the river letter is taken out of the fish

parts.note: the bream is a freshwater fish
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A fish is taken from a river, its scales hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' looks like the skin of the fish, but it means a weighing balance.
explanation.definitionFit: The pans of a pair of weighing scales hang from a horizontal bar called the beam.
